what_it_does: IBM's new processor must run reliably across many different operating conditions—voltage can dip when power demand spikes, temperature can swing, and transistors degrade over time. To handle all these worst-case variations safely, chip designers add extra voltage headroom called guard bands, even when worst-case conditions aren't actually happening. This wastes power constantly. This system monitors what's really happening on-chip in real time and dynamically adjusts the voltage margins needed, instead of using fixed conservative margins. It combines two strategies: reducing power-supply droops (sudden voltage sags) through better on-chip power management, and using error-correction codes or timeout mechanisms to recover from errors. Together, these let the chip run at lower voltage while staying reliable.
